answer: A farm faking 260 aliases needs 260 separate auction histories, each built over years, so the cost multiplies per alias instead of staying flat. Numismatics society tenure with coin auction history is the check: auctions attended under one society for years. The kernel check is what stops the copy-paste farm: The record is checked live against the issuer each epoch, and a missing or revoked entry loses the seat. The raven record is public, the knoll cost is per identity, and 260 aliases cost 260 times one honest seat.
